beats.narration: Checkpoint eight: three input scenarios, three encoding choices. If yours aren't picked yet, pause and decide first.

Scenario one: a reference product diagram used in every request your pipeline makes. Files API. Upload once, reference the file ID everywhere. Inline base sixty-four would re-send the same payload on every single call, paying transfer and latency each time for bytes Claude has already seen. Scenario two: a one-off screenshot of a UI bug, sent once by a support engineer. Inline base sixty-four. It's used exactly once, so an upload round-trip buys nothing. Encode it, send it, done. Scenario three: classifying five thousand customer feedback responses. The Message Batches API. One batch call, poll for completion, lower cost per token. A synchronous loop would either crawl through them one by one or slam thousands of connections into rate limits.

elements.text: ✓ Files API — base64 would re-pay per call
✓ inline base64 — an upload buys nothing here
✓ Batches — sync loop = crawl or rate-limit wall

beats.narration: The decision rule in one line: reuse decides the upload, volume decides the API. Reused asset: Files. Single use: inline. Thousands offline: batch. That's the last checkpoint of the module. Next: the wrap-up.
